chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ammar ibn Marwan from Sama'ah said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the food of the People of the Book, what is permissible from it? He said, 'Al-hubub (honey/sweeteners).'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What food of the People of the Book is permissible according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'al-hubub' (honey or sweet substances) is permissible for consumption from the People of the Book, distinguishing it from other food items that may require specific slaughter rites. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that honey, being a pure product not directly tied to the act of slaughter, is inherently clean (*tahir*) and thus exempt from the stricter conditions applied to meat. The narration underscores the principle of inherent purity in non-meat foodstuffs unless explicitly rendered impure by external factors.
